name: Failure Modes and Coordination Control
question: Why did the team loop, stall or overspend?
summary: Multi-agent teams repeat steps, miss stopping conditions, ignore each other, stop early or skip verification. The MAST study of over 1,600 traces sorts these into 14 modes in three categories. Coordination control answers them with hard caps on turns, tokens, time and depth, combined so that any one can stop the run, plus explicit stop signals, repetition detection and a verifier.
useCases: Any agent team that runs unattended: overnight, in CI, at scale
Budgets that must hold per run or per day

items.detail: system design ≈ 44%, inter-agent misalignment ≈ 32%, task verification ≈ 24%
step repetition 15.7%, reasoning–action mismatch 13.2%, unaware of stopping 12.4%
max_budget_usd ends the run and refuses new sub-agents
GraphRecursionError at the recursion limit (1000 by default from v1.0.6)

steps: Name one explicit stop signal, such as TERMINATE, and say when to use it
Add caps on messages, tokens and time, combined with OR
Detect repeated messages and intervene before the loop runs on
Verify with a real check before accepting done; return partial results with a reason
pitfalls: Combining caps with AND means none fires until all do
Caps set too tight cut legitimate long runs
A done claim without a check ships wrong output
remember: Any cap stops it. Nothing counts as done until checked.
caption: Illustrative: 4k tokens per message. Repetition is caught at message 9 and tests pass at message 12.

comparison.needs: Caps, a stop signal and a verifier

return True                  # same text twice in a row
# coder, model and run_tests are defined as usual
system_message="Call run_tests. Say APPROVED only if it returns PASS.")
result = await team.run(task="Fix the invoice rounding bug")

steps.title: Name the stop signal
steps.text: Agree on one explicit word, APPROVED, and say exactly when an agent may use it. Without one, a team has no way to say it is finished.

steps.title: Add hard caps
steps.text: Cap messages (30), tokens (100k) and wall time (12 minutes). Agents forget to stop; caps do not.

steps.title: Combine them with OR
steps.text: The | operator stops the run when any one condition fires. & would wait until all of them had fired, so a missing stop word could keep it running for ever.

steps.title: Detect repetition
steps.text: A custom condition compares each agent’s new message with its previous one. Here the coder resends the same patch at message 9, and the loop is caught.

steps.title: Verify before stopping
steps.text: The reviewer must run the tests and may say APPROVED only if they pass. At message 12 they do, so done means checked, not claimed.

steps.title: Return partial results with a reason
steps.text: If a cap or the loop check stops the run instead, return the last patch marked partial, with the stop reason, so a person can pick it up.

A verifier turns “done” into a checked result
cons: Caps set too tight cut legitimate long runs
More configuration to test and maintain

Do not use AND to combine safety caps

playgroundGuide.scenario: A SaaS firm runs 50 overnight coder–reviewer runs. A run needs 8 to 26 messages; each message costs 4k tokens and 20 seconds. Eight runs fall into a loop, re-sending the same patch; six claim APPROVED too early; and some agents simply forget to say APPROVED. Runs that nothing stops are killed by hand at 60 messages (240k tokens).
controls: Toggle message (30), token (100k, 25 messages) and time (12 minutes, 36 messages) caps.
Toggle a repetition detector and a verifier that runs the tests before APPROVED counts.
Choose AND or OR to combine the stop signal and caps, and set how often agents forget to say APPROVED.

presets.name: No stop rules
presets.expect: No caps: 15 of 50 runs never end (8 loops and 7 that never say APPROVED), 6 stop early on false claims, 35 outputs ship unchecked, and runs average 116.1k tokens (1.72× what the work needs).

presets.name: Caps combined with AND
presets.expect: All three caps, but with AND: still 15 endless runs, because AND waits for an APPROVED that never comes; the rest run on to message 36. 172.8k tokens per run (2.56×), 35 unverified.

presets.name: AND caps with a verifier
presets.expect: The verifier ends false claims and unverified outputs (0), but the 8 loops never pass their tests, so they are still endless under AND. 159.4k per run (2.36×).

presets.name: Repetition detector only
presets.expect: The detector breaks the 8 loops, but 7 runs that never say APPROVED are endless, 6 stop early and 43 outputs ship unchecked. 90.5k per run (1.34×).

missions.hint: Turn on at least one cap and combine with OR.

missions.text: With at least two caps on, keep premature stops at 2 or fewer and no endless runs.
missions.hint: False APPROVED claims and a tight token cap both stop runs too soon. The verifier catches one; the other is a cap to drop.

missions.text: With the verifier on, ship 0 unverified outputs at under 1.3× the base tokens, with no endless runs.
missions.hint: Verifier plus OR-combined caps (the detector helps too).

Explain why a verifier is needed before “done” counts

practice.scenario: A SaaS firm’s overnight coder and reviewer agents ping-ponged the same patch over a weekend and ran up USD 900. They now run with message, token and time caps combined with OR, a repetition check, and a verifier that runs the test suite before the reviewer may approve.

Agent teams that must hand back to a human after a fixed number of turns

practice.analogy: A cricket over. It ends after six legal balls, or earlier if the innings ends, whichever comes first; the umpire checks every appeal before the batter walks off.

library.name: AutoGen AgentChat
library.what: Built-in termination conditions that combine with | (either) and & (both). AutoGen is in maintenance mode; the same pattern exists in Microsoft Agent Framework.

practice.note: Replace the model name with a current one. Termination conditions receive only the messages since their last call, so the repetition check keeps the previous patch itself.

samples.code:
import asyncio, subprocess
from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_agentchat.teams import RoundRobinGroupChat
from autogen_agentchat.conditions import (
    TextMentionTermination, MaxMessageTermination, TokenUsageTermination,
    TimeoutTermination, FunctionalTermination)
from autogen_ext.models.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionClient

def run_tests() -> str:
    """Run the test suite and report PASS or FAIL."""
    r = subprocess.run(["pytest", "-q"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return "PASS" if r.returncode == 0 else "FAIL\n" + r.stdout[-2000:]

model = OpenAIChatCompletionClient(model="gpt-4.1-mini")
coder = AssistantAgent("coder", model_client=model,
                       system_message="Write the patch.")
reviewer = AssistantAgent("reviewer", model_client=model, tools=[run_tests],
                          system_message="Call run_tests. Say APPROVED only if it passes.")

last = {}
def repeated(msgs) -> bool:                # called with new messages only
    for m in msgs:
        if m.source == "coder":
            if last.get("coder") == m.to_text():
                return True                # same patch twice in a row
            last["coder"] = m.to_text()
    return False

stop = (TextMentionTermination("APPROVED")
        | MaxMessageTermination(30)
        | TokenUsageTermination(max_total_token=100_000)
        | TimeoutTermination(timeout_seconds=720)
        | FunctionalTermination(repeated))

team = RoundRobinGroupChat([coder, reviewer], termination_condition=stop)
result = asyncio.run(team.run(task="Fix the failing invoice-rounding test"))
print(result.stop_reason)

numericDrill.question: A coder–reviewer team uses 4k tokens per message. With OR-combined caps of 30 messages and 100k tokens, after how many messages does the run stop if nothing else stops it?
numericDrill.answer: The token cap is reached at 100k ÷ 4k = 25 messages, before the message cap of 30. With OR, the first cap reached stops the run, so it stops at 25 messages.

interview.question: Why combine termination conditions with OR rather than AND?
interview.answer: OR stops the run when any one cap is reached, so each cap is a real limit. AND waits until all conditions hold at once, so a run whose agents never say the stop word will never end.

interview.question: What are the three MAST failure categories?
interview.answer: System design issues (such as step repetition and unawareness of stopping conditions), inter-agent misalignment (such as ignoring another agent’s input or a reasoning–action mismatch) and task verification failures (such as stopping early or skipping checks).

mistakes.mistake: Don’t rely on agents to say when they are done.
mistakes.fix: Add hard caps on messages, tokens and time, combined with OR.
Run a verifier, such as the test suite, and return partial results with a stop reason.

quiz.question: A team uses TextMentionTermination("TERMINATE") & MaxMessageTermination(20). Neither agent ever says TERMINATE. What happens?
options: It never stops on its own, because & needs both conditions
It stops at the first message
It raises an error at once
quiz.explanation: & waits for both conditions; without TERMINATE it never fires. Use | so either one stops the run.

quiz.question: Each message uses about 4k tokens. Caps of 30 messages and 100k tokens are combined with OR. After how many messages does the run stop, if nothing else stops it?
quiz.explanation: The token cap is reached at 100k ÷ 4k = 25 messages, before the message cap.

quiz.question: Which are categories in the MAST taxonomy of multi-agent failures? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: MAST’s three categories are system design, inter-agent misalignment and task verification. Hardware and security issues are outside it.

quiz.question: According to MAST, which single failure mode is most common?
quiz.explanation: Step repetition is the most common at about 15.7%, ahead of reasoning–action mismatch (13.2%) and unawareness of stopping conditions (12.4%).

quiz.question: A coder–reviewer loop runs for 180 messages of about 5k tokens each. At USD 10 per million tokens, what does it cost?
quiz.explanation: 180 × 5k = 900k tokens; 900k × USD 10 per million = USD 9.

quiz.question: A Claude Agent SDK research run reaches max_budget_usd. What happens?
options: It keeps going and bills later
New sub-agents are refused and the query ends with an error_max_budget_usd result
quiz.explanation: The SDK enforces the cap: it refuses new sub-agents, stops background ones and ends the query.

quiz.question: A bank’s overnight reconciliation team needs stop rules. Which belong in the design? Select all that apply.
options: An explicit stop signal that agents are told when to use
Caps on messages, tokens and time, combined with OR
A verifier that checks the result before it counts as done
Caps combined with AND so every limit is respected
quiz.explanation: A stop signal, OR-combined caps and a verifier bound the run and make done mean checked. AND lets a run continue until every condition has fired.

quiz.question: A LangGraph agent loop exceeds its recursion limit. What happens?
options: The graph silently stops and returns the last state
The limit resets and the loop continues
The graph switches to a smaller model
quiz.explanation: Reaching the recursion limit raises GraphRecursionError, which you can catch and handle.

quiz.question: Which OpenAI Agents SDK setting bounds the whole agent loop, including handoffs?
quiz.explanation: max_turns caps the loop; passing it raises MaxTurnsExceeded.

quiz.question: Messages take about 20 seconds each. A TimeoutTermination of 12 minutes corresponds to about how many messages?
quiz.explanation: 12 minutes = 720 seconds ÷ 20 = 36 messages.

quiz.question: You write a custom repetition check as an AutoGen FunctionalTermination. What must it do? Select all that apply.
options: Compare each agent’s new message with that agent’s previous one
Keep its own record of earlier messages, because it receives only new ones
Delete earlier messages from the chat
quiz.explanation: Termination conditions see only messages since their last call, so a repetition check keeps its own state and compares.

quiz.question: After adding a 20-message cap, 12% of legitimate refactor runs are cut off before finishing. What is the best response?
options: Set the cap from the distribution of successful runs, for example just above the longest normal run, and return partial work when it fires
quiz.explanation: Caps should bound failures, not normal work. Size them from real run lengths and return partial results with a reason.

quiz.question: A reviewer agent approves patches without running the tests, and broken code ships. Which MAST category is this?
options: None; it is a model bug
quiz.explanation: Skipping or weakening checks is a task-verification failure. Require a verifier, such as the test suite, before approval counts.

quiz.question: Of 50 runs, 8 never stop and are killed at 240k tokens; the other 42 average 70k. What is the average tokens per run?
A cap fires before a catalogue-cleanup team finishes. What should the caller receive? Select all that apply.
options: The partial result produced so far
The stop reason, such as which cap fired
The reviewer’s last APPROVED message, presented as final
An empty result, so no partial data is exposed
quiz.explanation: Partial work plus the reason lets a person continue. Presenting an unchecked message as final, or returning nothing, hides the failure.

quiz.question: Which AutoGen condition stops a team when prompt or completion tokens pass a limit?
quiz.explanation: TokenUsageTermination watches token usage; MaxMessageTermination counts messages.

quiz.question: The MAST study reports κ = 0.88 for its annotations. What does that number measure?
options: Agreement between human annotators labelling the failures
quiz.explanation: Cohen’s kappa measures inter-annotator agreement; 0.88 is strong agreement on the taxonomy.

quiz.question: A team combines “says DONE” AND MaxMessageTermination(30). An agent says DONE at message 12. When does the run stop?
options: At message 30, when both conditions have fired
quiz.explanation: With AND, each condition must have fired; DONE fired at 12 and the message cap fires at 30, so the run wastes 18 messages.

quiz.question: Which controls act on the team as a whole rather than on one agent’s prompt? Select all that apply.
options: A cap on sub-agent nesting depth
A spend cap for the whole run
quiz.explanation: Depth, concurrency and team-wide spend caps bound the team. Prompt length is a single-agent control.

quiz.question: Adding up MAST’s per-mode shares, which category accounts for the largest share of failures?
quiz.explanation: System design issues, such as step repetition and unawareness of stopping conditions, add up to about 44%.
